issues.legal_issue: Allowing review of a decree vacates and supersedes the original decree.
material_facts: A court allowed an application to review an original decree and then issued a new decree changing the compensation awarded.
issues.conclusion: The decree passed on review was a new decree that superseded the original decree, whether it modified, reversed, or confirmed it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the established rule that allowing review vacates the original decree and the decree subsequently passed on review supersedes it. It relied on Nibaran Chandra Sikdar v. Abdul Hakim, Kanhaiya Lal v. Baldev Prasad, Brijbaso Lal v. Salig Ram, and Pyari Mohan Kundu v. Kalu Khan; the review application had been made under Order 47, Rule 1 of the Civil Procedure Code.

predicates.a_review_proceeding_was_decided: A court considered an application to review a decree.
predicates.review_application_was_allowed: The court granted the application to review the decree.

issues.definition: When a court grants review of a decree, the decree subsequently made on review supersedes the original decree.

issues.legal_issue: When a review is held to have been wrongly allowed, the original decree is restored and becomes final if the party seeking to challenge it did not appeal that decree.
material_facts: A court allowed a review application and replaced an original decree with a decree reducing the compensation.
The party that obtained review appealed from the decree made on review but did not appeal the original decree.
The opposing party filed a cross-appeal challenging the review.
The appellate court held that the review had been wrongly allowed but dismissed both appeals, leaving the decree made on review in place.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court should have allowed the cross-appeal and dismissed the appeal from the decree made on review. The original decree was restored and, because it had not been appealed, had become final.
issues.legal_principle: Because the decree made on review superseded the original decree, an appeal from that later decree was not an appeal from the original decree. Once the review was held to have been wrongly allowed, the original decree revived; without an appeal against it, that decree became final. The Court applied the review principle supported by Nibaran Chandra Sikdar v. Abdul Hakim, Kanhaiya Lal v. Baldev Prasad, Brijbaso Lal v. Salig Ram, and Pyari Mohan Kundu v. Kalu Khan.

rule.if: an_appeal_from_a_review_decree_was_before_the_appellate_court and the_review_was_held_improper and the_original_decree_was_not_appealed and a_cross_appeal_challenged_the_review

predicates.an_appeal_from_a_review_decree_was_befor: A party appealed from a decree made after a court had reviewed an earlier decree.
predicates.the_review_was_held_improper: The appellate court concluded that the review had been wrongly allowed.
predicates.the_original_decree_was_not_appealed: The party seeking to challenge the original decree did not appeal that decree.
predicates.a_cross_appeal_challenged_the_review: The opposing party filed a cross-appeal challenging the decision to allow review.

issues.definition: If an appellate court finds a review improper, the original decree was not appealed, and a cross-appeal challenges the review, the original decree is restored and final.
